explanation: Lufthansa Group and closely aligned Central European legacy carriers built around major hub-and-spoke operations such as Frankfurt, Munich, Zurich, Vienna, and Brussels.
Air France-KLM group carriers centered on the Paris and Amsterdam hub systems, representing a major Northwest European legacy network pattern.
IAG-related legacy traffic, mainly British Airways, Iberia, and Aer Lingus, associated with Heathrow-, Madrid-, and Dublin-linked network flows.
Northern European network and flag carriers with Scandinavian, Finnish, and Baltic-oriented route structures.
Southern European flag and network carriers, especially relevant for Iberian, Italian, and Portuguese flows within Europe.
Large legacy carriers connecting Europe with Turkey and Southeastern Europe, often mixing intra-European and broader connecting flows.
Ryanair and related operational prefixes. This group captures one of the dominant European low-cost point-to-point traffic patterns and should remain isolated.
easyJet family low-cost traffic, including multiple operational prefixes, representing dense intra-European scheduled point-to-point service.
Wizz Air traffic, especially relevant for Central, Eastern, and Southeastern European low-cost connectivity.
Other low-cost, leisure, and charter airlines not belonging to the main Ryanair, easyJet, or Wizz families. This bucket captures residual point-to-point and holiday-oriented traffic.
Dedicated cargo, freight, and parcel operators, including both express integrators and classical cargo airlines. These routes follow very different operational logic from passenger airlines.
Business aviation, regional carriers, and smaller specialized commercial operators that are too sparse to model separately but still distinct from the main legacy and low-cost airline families.
